hints: Focus on what bonding electrons mean, each single bond holds 2 electrons, a double bond holds 4.
Count the bonds in each molecule first, remember $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ has a C=C double bond plus four C-H bonds.
Look for the molecule with exactly three single bonds and no multiple bonds, that gives 3 x 2 bonding electrons.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as bonding electrons**

Remember, bonding electrons are the electrons shared in covalent bonds. Each single bond uses 2 electrons.

Rule to use:
$$\text{bonding electrons} = 2 \times (\text{number of single bonds}) + 4 \times (\text{number of double bonds})$$

**Draw the bonding in each molecule**

Let us count bonds quickly. $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ has 2 single bonds, $\text{NCl}_3$ has 3 single bonds, $\text{SF}_6$ has 6 single bonds.

For $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ (ethene): $$\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$$ It has 4 C-H single bonds plus 1 C=C double bond.

**Convert bonds to electrons and decide**

Now multiply by 2 per single bond and 4 for the double bond. $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ has 4, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ has 12, $\text{SF}_6$ has 12.

Only $\text{NCl}_3$ has 3 single bonds, so $3 \times 2 = 6$ bonding electrons, which matches the question.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ has four C-H single bonds (8 electrons) plus one C=C double bond (4 electrons), giving 12 bonding electrons in total, not 6.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ is H-S-H with two single bonds only, so it has 2 x 2 = 4 bonding electrons.
options.C: Correct. $\text{NCl}_3$ has nitrogen bonded to three chlorines by three single N-Cl bonds, with a lone pair left on N. So bonding electrons = 3 x 2 = 6.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{SF}_6$ has six S-F single bonds around sulfur, so it has 6 x 2 = 12 bonding electrons. Students sometimes confuse number of bonds with number of electrons.
